correctness.rationale: A group containing the unique largest divisor m! must have total at least m!, hence five-layered implies sigma(m!)/m!≥5. This abundancy quotient is monotone under divisibility, so all m≤13 fail once sigma(13!)=31044179712<5·13!=31135104000 is checked. At 14!, sigma=442487616480, equal group sum T=88497523296. I independently parsed all four explicit supplied divisor lists (lengths 5,7,10,27), tested all 49 entries are pairwise distinct positive divisors of 14!, summed each exactly to T, and used tau(14!)=2592 to show the nonempty complement of 2543 divisors sums to T. This proves the complete minimality assertion, not just a finite sample.
